title: PhasePilot: Muse Closes the Loop on PhaseScan

beats.heading: PhasePilot
beats.subtitle: Muse (muse-spark-1.3) decides, SAM checks, a Bayesian planner maps
beats.presenter: PhasePilot hands a real phase-mapping experiment to Muse and lets it run the loop live.
Condensates organise the cell by phase separation, and every protein has its own phase diagram to map.

beats.heading: PhaseScan on Beta3
bullets: Beta3 microfluidic rig in our Cambridge lab, filmed today
Syringe pumps blend protein, RNA, crowder and buffer on chip
Each 100 pL droplet holds one condition to test
beats.note: Real footage: rig door, syringe pumps and chip stage in sequence.
beats.presenter: This is the real Beta3 rig at Transition Bio that will run the experiment you are about to see.
A droplet uses about a million times less protein, yet the search explodes, so Muse, SAM and the Bayesian planner divide the work.

beats.heading: Live today on Beta3
bullets: Live run, 4 November 2026: G3BP1 / PolyA RNA / PEG
Muse picked each setpoint from live evidence and said why
SAM outlined every droplet; only passing images count
beats.note: The dashboard on the rig monitor during today's run, not a mock-up.
beats.presenter: Today this loop ran live on G3BP1, PolyA RNA and PEG, with every decision made from the evidence as it arrived.
Here is the real dashboard in four parts: decisions, Muse's reasoning, SAM quality control and the growing map.
SAM ViT-B outlines every droplet frame, green for accepted and red for rejected, so bad images never become results.
Muse reads the accumulated evidence and writes down why this setpoint, and not another, is worth testing next.
Each accepted result redraws the Bayesian phase map and moves the predicted boundary, shown dashed, to where sampling should go next.

beats.heading: Biology is high-n
bullets: Protein, RNA, crowder, salt, pH, compound, temperature
beats.note: Every extra variable multiplies a raster scan, so the loop must hunt the boundary instead.
beats.presenter: Real biology adds variable after variable, which is exactly where a boundary-hunting loop earns its keep.

beats.heading: Measured gains

stats.line: less protein to map the phase boundary

stats.sub: Pumps and camera busy 2.9 min instead of 51 min

stats.line: extra variables in the same instrument time and protein
stats.sub: +1 at 10 levels per variable; +2 at 4 levels per variable

beats.note: Wall clock was 23 min: 7 rounds each waited 180 s for incubation while pumps idled; keeping droplets flowing brings it to 2.9 min.
beats.footnote: Source: 3-variable replay (G3BP1 / TDP-43 / RNA, 180 s incubation); boundary accuracy at or above 0.997 vs the full scan.
beats.green_line: A 17x saving buys log_k(17) extra dimensions at every n: raster costs k^n, the loop samples the n-1 boundary at ~k^(n-1).
beats.presenter: Against the full scan we measured twenty times less protein, seventeen times less instrument time, and one to two extra variables mapped.
One closed loop can now be pointed at any protein and any parameter space we choose to explore.
